jess: heads-up: I ran the kernel-selector rollout on staging (kernel-chooser v2). seeing weird batch formation on L4 — lots of tiny batches and higher KV cache miss rate. p95 latency up ~18% for short prompts. numbers below.

jess: ```
GPU   | p50  | p95  | avg_batch_tokens | kv_hit
L4    | 72ms | 280ms | 32              | 0.62
A10   | 60ms | 220ms | 80              | 0.88
H100  | 45ms | 160ms | 128             | 0.94
```

cheng: interesting — the selector seems to favor small-token kernels (id 17) when seq_len<=32. that + current batcher policy means requests aren't being merged before scheduling. can you paste the selector trace for one of the slow batches?

jess: trace snippet: ```selector:choose(requests=[r1(20),r2(12),r3(8)]) -> pick kernel 17 for all; batcher: split into slots 2/1 -> dispatch to gpu0,gpu1; kv_cache_miss: r2,r3 miss (prefixs not shared)```

rahul: two levers here: 1) make kernel selector less aggressive about choosing tiny-kernel for mixed batches, or 2) tune batcher to increase max_tokens_per_batch for L4 so it packs more short requests together. quick proposal: bump L4 max_tokens_per_batch 256 -> 512 and add kernel-fallback threshold at 40 tokens. rollback if regressions show.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created canary config `batch-l4-bump-512` -> /canaries/1717776543. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/kernel-batcher/pull/1423 :rocket:

sam: also watch KV cache fragmentation metrics — more tiny batches => less KV reuse. suggest enabling prefix_caching=true for short prompts in the canary to reduce misses.

dave: I'll run a synthetic perf sweep (10k short prompts, seq_len 8-32) against the canary vs baseline and post kv_hit/p95/delta by EOD. assigning to myself.

jess: :thumbsup: thanks. if canary shows p95 delta <5% and kv_hit improves, we can roll to staging and then prod. will also add a short runbook for per-GPU max_tokens tuning (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100) after results.
